---
title: "CodeClimateCorrelation"
subtitle: "Moving-window climate response surfaces, one site at a time"
format: html
editor: visual
---

This document reproduces the **first analytical section of `CodeMain.qmd`** --
everything up to and including *Moving-window climate correlations* -- for all
six sites that have crossdated cores (AMI, GHE, KAT, LIN, STO, TRO) instead of
for Ghent alone. Nothing that follows that section in `CodeMain.qmd`
(extreme-year selection, drought progression, growth in the extreme years, the
built-up GLMM) is reproduced here.

What changed relative to `CodeMain.qmd`, and why:

- **The `# Only Ghent for now` filter is gone.** Everything up to the
  chronologies now runs once on the full dataset, and the site becomes a
  grouping variable (`Site`, the first three characters of `TreeID`) from the
  chronologies onwards.
- **Chronologies are built per site x species**, and the replication floor is a
  setting (`MIN_REPL`) rather than the hard-coded `BBI_n >= 10`. Ghent has
  69-99 crossdated trees per species; the other five sites have 5-8, so a floor
  of 10 would silently return five empty chronologies. The realised replication
  is printed per site so it is visible what each surface rests on.
- **Latitude and elevation are per site.** `SITE_LAT`/`SITE_ELEV` were two
  scalars; extraterrestrial radiation changes by roughly 10 % per 5 degrees of
  latitude, and these sites span 49.99 N to 63.45 N, so one shared value would
  bias PET badly for Trondheim.
- **The daily climate and the response surfaces are computed in a loop over
  sites**, and both are cached to disk. Re-running the document does not
  recompute a site whose correlation field is already on disk unless
  `RECOMPUTE` is `TRUE`.
- Two small robustness fixes that the single-site version did not need: the
  `Species` spellings in `Trees_Cooltree.xlsx` are normalised before the
  shrinkage join (the sheet contains both `Fraxinus exelsior` and
  `Fraxinus excelsior`, and both `Tillia` and `Tilia`; a typo would join to
  `Sr = NA` and take out `bakker_bai()` with an opaque error), and the ERA5
  readers resolve their own file names and trim incomplete days at either end
  of the record rather than hard-coding `>= 1940-01-02`.

The output is one correlation field per site, saved as
`Output/ClimateCorrelation/<SITE>/ClimCor_<SITE>.rds`, plus a combined
`ClimCor_AllSites.rds` for the sections that will follow.

# Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}

#### clear global environment ####
remove(list = ls())

#### load necessary (and usefull) packages ####
library("dplR")       # dendrochronology
library("tidyverse")  # data manipulation
library("dplyr")      # data manipulation
library("ggplot2")    # plotting
library("readxl")     # read xlsx files
library("writexl")    # write xlsx files
library("ggpubr")     # arrange ggplots
library("mgcv")       # GAM (generalized additive model)

#### load XCT.Read function ####
source("XCT.Read.R")

```

# Site configuration

```{r sites}

# The six sites that have crossdated cores. `Site` is the first three
# characters of every TreeID at that site and the suffix of the ERA5 file;
# `Region` is the spelling used in Trees_Cooltree.xlsx. The three regions in
# the metadata with no cored trees (Alnarp, Bremen, Potsdam) drop out by
# themselves at the Cored/Crossdate_Status filter and are deliberately absent
# here, so a new site appearing in the tree-ring data raises an error instead
# of quietly running without a latitude.
#
# Lat/Lon are the mean coordinates of that site's trees, and Lat is only a
# FALLBACK: if the ERA5 csv still carries its own `latitude` column, the
# grid-cell latitude from the file is used instead, because that is the
# latitude the climate series actually belongs to.
#
# Elev is approximate. It enters only the clear-sky reference radiation Rso
# and the psychrometric constant, both weakly (FAO-56), so a rough figure is
# fine -- but it is per site rather than one shared number, because Katowice
# sits some 260 m above the other five.
SITES <- tribble(
  ~Site, ~Region,      ~Lat,    ~Lon,     ~Elev,
  "AMI", "Amiens",     49.9878,  2.3582,   35,
  "GHE", "Ghent",      51.0506,  3.7206,   10,
  "KAT", "Katowice",   50.4520, 18.7579,  270,
  "LIN", "Linkoping",  58.4084, 15.5654,   55,
  "STO", "Stockholm",  59.4410, 18.0915,   30,
  "TRO", "Trondheim",  63.4520, 10.5375,   30
)

#### paths ####
dataFolder             <- "Data/TreeRingData/Raw_100dens_30area"
removeDensityRingsPath <- "Data/TreeRingData/rings not usable for density mesurements.xlsx"
metaDataPath           <- "Data/TreeRingData/Trees_Cooltree.xlsx"
climDir                <- "Data/ClimateData"
outRoot                <- "Output/ClimateCorrelation"

dir.create(outRoot, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

#### chronology settings ####

# Replication floor. CodeMain used 10, which is right for Ghent (69-99
# crossdated trees per species) and empties every other site (5-8 per
# species). Lower it and the surfaces exist but rest on fewer trees; raise it
# and the non-Ghent sites disappear. Whatever it is set to, the realised
# replication is printed below.
MIN_REPL <- 5

# ERA5 starts in 1940, so nothing before it can be correlated with climate.
FIRST_YEAR <- 1940

# A site x species chronology shorter than this cannot reach `MIN_N`
# overlapping years in any window, so it is dropped before the correlations
# rather than producing an all-NA surface.
MIN_YEARS <- 25

#### recompute or reuse ####

# The correlation fields are expensive (see the timing note in the
# correlations chunk). Set to TRUE to force a recompute; FALSE reuses any
# ClimCor_<SITE>.rds already on disk.
RECOMPUTE <- FALSE

#### find each site's ERA5 file ####

# The file naming is resolved rather than assumed, because CodeMain read
# "ERA5-Ghent.csv" and the six-site set is named "ERA5_AMI" etc.
era5_path <- function(site, region, dir = climDir) {

  cand <- file.path(dir, c(
    paste0("ERA5_", site,   ".csv"),
    paste0("ERA5-", site,   ".csv"),
    paste0("ERA5_", region, ".csv"),
    paste0("ERA5-", region, ".csv"),
    paste0("ERA5",  site,   ".csv")
  ))

  hit <- cand[file.exists(cand)]

  if (!length(hit)) {
    stop("No ERA5 file found for site ", site, " (", region, ").\n  Tried:\n    ",
         paste(cand, collapse = "\n    "),
         "\n  Files present in ", dir, ":\n    ",
         paste(list.files(dir), collapse = "\n    "))
  }

  hit[1]
}

# Resolve all six now: a typo should fail in two seconds, not after the
# tree-ring pipeline has run.
SITES <- SITES %>%
  mutate(ClimPath = purrr::map2_chr(Site, Region, era5_path))

SITES

```

# Load and filter data

```{r}

# Load RW and mean ring density
Data <- XCT.read(
  path = dataFolder,
  output = "ringwidth_density",
  densityType = "fraction",
  area = c(0, 1),
  fun = "mean") %>%
  mutate(TreeID = substr(Sample, 1, 8)) %>%
  na.omit()


# remove -A and -B at the end of split Samples
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(Sample = str_remove(Sample, "-A$")) %>%
  mutate(Sample = str_remove(Sample, "-B$"))


# remove density of rings with non usefull density data, make those NA
Data <- Data %>%
  full_join(read_excel(removeDensityRingsPath), by = c("Sample", "Year")) %>%
  mutate(Density = ifelse(!is.na(`Reason`), NA, Density)) %>%
  select(-c(`Reason`))


# add temparary species column
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(
    species_temp = substr(Sample, 5, 5),
    species_temp = recode(
      species_temp,
      "Q" = "Quercus",
      "T" = "Tilia",
      "F" = "Fraxinus"
    )
  )


# what came in, per site
Data %>%
  mutate(Site = substr(Sample, 1, 3)) %>%
  group_by(Site, species_temp) %>%
  summarise(n_samples = n_distinct(Sample), n_rings = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = species_temp, values_from = c(n_samples, n_rings)) %>%
  print(n = 30)


# plot density vs RW, one panel per species
p1 <- ggplot(Data[is.na(Data$Density)==FALSE, ], aes(x = RW, y = Density)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~species_temp) +
  labs(x = "Ring Width (mm)", y = "Mean Ring Density (kg/m³)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA))

p2 <- ggplot(Data[is.na(Data$Density)==FALSE, ], aes(x = RW)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.5, boundary = 0 , fill = "lightblue", color = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~species_temp) +
  labs(x = "Ring Width (mm)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, NA))

ggarrange(p1, p2, ncol = 1, heights = c(2, 1))

```

# average years per tree

```{r}

# average per year
Data <- Data %>%
  group_by(Year, TreeID, species_temp) %>%
  summarise(
    RW = if (all(is.na(RW))) NA_real_ else mean(RW, na.rm = TRUE),
    Density = if (all(is.na(Density))) NA_real_ else mean(Density, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```

# fill missing density values

One GAM per species, fitted on all sites at once -- as in `CodeMain.qmd`, where
the imputation also ran before the Ghent filter. The density-ring-width
relationship is a wood property, not a site property, so pooling is deliberate:
it also means the imputation for a 7-tree site borrows the shape of the
Ghent curve instead of fitting one to almost nothing.

```{r}

# Fit GAM for each species
models <- Data %>%
  filter(!is.na(RW), !is.na(Density)) %>%
  group_by(species_temp) %>%
  group_split() %>%
  setNames(unique(Data$species_temp)) %>%
  lapply(function(dat) {
    gam(
      Density ~ s(RW, k = 6),
      data = dat,
      method = "REML"
    )
  })

# predict density for the missing values
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(Density_imputed = is.na(Density)) %>%
  group_by(species_temp) %>%
  group_modify(~ {

    model <- models[[unique(.y$species_temp)]]

    .x$Density_predicted <- predict(
      model,
      newdata = .x
    )

    .x$Density <- ifelse(
      is.na(.x$Density) & !is.na(.x$RW),
      .x$Density_predicted,
      .x$Density
    )

    .x
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# plot the models
ggplot(Data, aes(RW, Density)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(shape = Density_imputed),
    alpha = 0.5,
    size = 1
  ) +
  geom_smooth(
    data = Data %>% filter(!Density_imputed),
    method = "gam",
    formula = y ~ s(x, k = 6),
    se = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~species_temp, scales = "free_y") +
  theme_bw()

# how much was imputed, per site
Data %>%
  mutate(Site = substr(TreeID, 1, 3)) %>%
  group_by(Site) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), imputed = sum(Density_imputed),
            pct_imputed = round(100 * mean(Density_imputed), 1),
            .groups = "drop")

# remove density_predicted
Data$Density_predicted <- NULL

```

# add metadata

```{r}

# load tree metadata, calculate diameter and barkless diameter and add to Data
metaData <- read_excel(metaDataPath) %>%
  rename(TreeID = `Tree`)

metaData <- metaData %>%
  mutate(DBH_mm = Circumference_Drilling_Height_mm / pi) %>%
  mutate(Barkless_DBH_mm = DBH_mm - Single_Bark_Thickness_mm * 2) %>%
  select(-c(Circumference_Drilling_Height_mm))

Data <- Data %>%
  left_join(metaData, by = c("TreeID"))

# remove trees that were not cored or did not crossdate
Data <- Data %>%
  filter(Cored == "YES", Crossdate_Status == "Yes") %>%
  select(-c(Cored, Crossdate_Status))

# remove non useful columns
Data <- Data %>%
  select(-c(Circumference_Breast_Height_AstridVDB_mm, Remarks, Last_Complete_Ring, Logger_Data_Present_AstridVandenbossche, Soil_Data_present_AstridVandenbossche, LIDAR_data_Present_KarlienMoeys, Dendrometer_Data_Present_KarenDePauw, Owner, Email, Phone, species_temp))


#### site column, and the check that makes it trustworthy ####

# `Site` is derived from the TreeID rather than from `Region`, so it cannot
# disagree with the ERA5 file it selects. The cross-check below is what
# catches a mislabelled tree: a TreeID whose prefix does not match its
# Region, or a site present in the data but absent from SITES.
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(Site = substr(TreeID, 1, 3))

site_check <- Data %>%
  distinct(Site, Region) %>%
  full_join(SITES %>% select(Site, Region_cfg = Region), by = "Site")

if (any(is.na(site_check$Region) | is.na(site_check$Region_cfg) |
        site_check$Region != site_check$Region_cfg)) {
  print(site_check)
  stop("Site/Region mismatch: every site in the data needs exactly one row in ",
       "SITES with the same Region. Add the site (with its latitude and ",
       "elevation) or fix the TreeID prefix.")
}

# unify Site to a factor in SITES order, so every table and facet strip below
# reads west-to-east / south-to-north in the same order
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(Site = factor(Site, levels = SITES$Site))

Data %>%
  group_by(Site, Region) %>%
  summarise(n_trees = n_distinct(TreeID), n_rings = n(),
            first_year = min(Year), last_year = max(Year), .groups = "drop")

```

# correct RW and density for shrinkage: species-specific total radial shrinkage for ring width, and species-specific total volumetric shrinkage for density. based on CIRAD Tropix sheets and GWDD database

```{r}

# Trees_Cooltree.xlsx spells two of the three species inconsistently
# ("Fraxinus exelsior" alongside "Fraxinus excelsior", "Tillia x europaea"
# alongside "Tilia x europaea"). With Ghent alone that never mattered; across
# six sites a typo would join to Sr = NA, propagate into RW_green, and surface
# only as bakker_bai()'s "Required columns contain NA values". Normalise
# first, then assert the join was complete.
Data <- Data %>%
  mutate(Species = recode(
    Species,
    "Fraxinus exelsior" = "Fraxinus excelsior",
    "Tillia x europaea" = "Tilia x europaea"
  ))

# Species-specific shrinkage coefficients, based on CIRAD Tropix sheets and GWDD
shrinkage <- tibble(
  Species = c(
    "Fraxinus excelsior",
    "Quercus robur",
    "Tilia x europaea"
  ),

  # total green -> oven-dry radial shrinkage
  Sr = c(
    0.057,
    0.045,
    0.050
  ),

  # volumetric shrinkage used for density correction
  Sv = c(
    0.1475,
    0.1376,
    0.1200
  )
)


Data <- Data %>%
  left_join(shrinkage, by = "Species") %>%
  mutate(

    # oven-dry ring width -> reconstructed green ring width
    RW_green = RW / (1 - Sr),

    # oven-dry density -> basic density
    # i.e. oven-dry mass / green volume
    Density_basic = Density * (1 - Sv)

  )

if (anyNA(Data$Sr)) {
  print(Data %>% filter(is.na(Sr)) %>% distinct(Site, Species))
  stop("Species without shrinkage coefficients: add them to `shrinkage` or ",
       "add the spelling to the recode above.")
}

Data <- Data %>% select(-c(Sr, Sv))

```

# Basal area geometry (Bakker method)

`BAI_mm2` survives only because the basal biomass increment of the next chunk is `BAI x basic density`; nothing downstream analyses it. From the chronologies onwards the response variable is BBI.

```{r}


bakker_bai <- function(data) {
  
  # Required columns
  required_cols <- c(
    "TreeID",
    "Year",
    "RW_green",
    "Barkless_DBH_mm",
    "Distance_to_Pith_mm"
  )
  
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(data))
  
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Missing required columns: ",
      paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }
  
  # Check for missing values in variables needed for calculation
  if (anyNA(data[, required_cols])) {
    stop("Required columns contain NA values.")
  }
  
  # Check ring widths
  if (any(data$RW_green < 0)) {
    stop("RW_green cannot contain negative values.")
  }
  
  # Sort chronologically within tree
  data <- data[
    order(data$TreeID, data$Year),
  ]
  
  # Check that DBH and distance-to-pith are constant within tree
  dbh_n <- tapply(
    data$Barkless_DBH_mm,
    data$TreeID,
    function(x) length(unique(x))
  )
  
  d2p_n <- tapply(
    data$Distance_to_Pith_mm,
    data$TreeID,
    function(x) length(unique(x))
  )
  
  if (any(dbh_n > 1)) {
    stop("Barkless_DBH_mm must be constant within each TreeID.")
  }
  
  if (any(d2p_n > 1)) {
    stop("Distance_to_Pith_mm must be constant within each TreeID.")
  }
  
  # Split by tree
  out <- lapply(
    split(data, data$TreeID),
    function(x) {
      
      # Current inside-bark DBH
      dbh_current <- x$Barkless_DBH_mm[1]
      
      # Distance from innermost measured ring to estimated pith
      d2p <- x$Distance_to_Pith_mm[1]
      
      # Chronological radius represented by the core:
      #
      # estimated unmeasured distance to pith
      # +
      # all measured ring widths
      I_P <- d2p + sum(x$RW_green)
      
      if (I_P <= 0) {
        stop(
          "Total chronological radius must be > 0 for TreeID ",
          x$TreeID[1]
        )
      }
      
      # Radius accumulated BEFORE each measured ring
      radial_start <- d2p + c(
        0,
        head(cumsum(x$RW_green), -1)
      )
      
      # Radius accumulated through the END of each measured ring
      radial_end <- d2p + cumsum(x$RW_green)
      
      # Bakker proportional factors
      G_start <- radial_start / I_P
      G_end   <- radial_end   / I_P
      
      # Reconstructed inside-bark diameter
      DBH_start <- dbh_current * G_start
      DBH_end   <- dbh_current * G_end
      
      # Basal area (mm^2)
      BA_start <- pi * (DBH_start / 2)^2
      BA_end   <- pi * (DBH_end / 2)^2
      
      # Annual basal area increment
      BAI <- BA_end - BA_start
      
      # Add results
      x$BA_startyear_mm2 <- BA_start
      x$BAI_mm2 <- BAI
      
      x
    }
  )
  
  # Return long-format dataframe
  out <- do.call(rbind, out)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  
  out
}


Data <- bakker_bai(Data)



# No BAI diagnostics here on purpose: BAI is an intermediate now, so the
# increment-against-size plots live in the BBI chunk below and nowhere else.


```

# BBI calculations

```{r}

# density is in kg/m³, we need to convert it to g/mm³
Data$Density_gmm3 <- Data$Density_basic / 1000000

# calculate BBI (basal biomass increment) in g/mm
Data$BBI_gmm <- Data$BAI_mm2 * Data$Density_gmm3




# plot
ggplot(Data, aes(x = BA_startyear_mm2, y = BBI_gmm)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_grid(Species ~ Region) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1000000), ylim = c(0, 30))

# per site, on its own scale: the non-Ghent sites are 5-8 trees each and
# would be invisible inside a shared axis range
ggplot(Data, aes(x = BA_startyear_mm2, y = BBI_gmm)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.5, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~Site, scales = "free") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


```

determine cambial age and cut first years

```{r}

#| label: cambial-age

#' Add cambial age to a long-format tree-ring dataframe
#'
#' CambialAge_measured : ring index counting from the innermost MEASURED ring
#'                       (= 1 for that ring). This is exact but underestimates
#'                       true cambial age whenever the core missed the pith.
#'
#' PithOffset_est      : estimated number of unmeasured rings between pith and
#'                       innermost measured ring, from Distance_to_Pith_mm
#'                       divided by the mean width of the innermost `n_inner`
#'                       measured rings (sensu the linear-extrapolation
#'                       approach; cf. Duncan 1989 for the geometric
#'                       alternative based on arc curvature).
#'
#' CambialAge         : CambialAge_measured + PithOffset_est, rounded.

n_inner <- 10   # rings used to estimate the near-pith growth rate

Data <- Data %>%
  arrange(TreeID, Year) %>%
  group_by(TreeID) %>%
  mutate(
    CambialAge_measured = row_number(),
    
    # mean width of the innermost measured rings (green/shrinkage-corrected,
    # to match the units of Distance_to_Pith_mm)
    RW_inner_mean = mean(RW_green[CambialAge_measured <= n_inner], na.rm = TRUE),
    
    PithOffset_est = if_else(
      is.na(Distance_to_Pith_mm) | RW_inner_mean <= 0,
      NA_real_,
      round(Distance_to_Pith_mm / RW_inner_mean)
    ),
    
    CambialAge = CambialAge_measured + coalesce(PithOffset_est, 0),
    
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-RW_inner_mean)


# how much of the collection is affected, and by how much
Data %>%
  group_by(Site, TreeID, Species) %>%
  summarise(
    d2p_mm    = first(Distance_to_Pith_mm),
    offset    = first(PithOffset_est),
    n_rings   = n(),
    first_yr  = min(Year),
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(offset)) %>%
  print(n = 20)


# cut first x years of each tree
nyears_cut <- 15
Data <- Data %>% 
  filter(CambialAge > nyears_cut)

# remove samples with less then x years left
nyears_min <- 5
Data <- Data %>%
  group_by(TreeID) %>%
  filter(n() >= nyears_min) %>%
  ungroup()


```

# detrend BBI

Primary: Cook & Peters (1997), The Holocene 7:361–370. This is the citation for transform-then-subtract. Log is their p = 0 case, so cite it as such rather than implying they recommend log unconditionally — something like “following Cook and Peters (1997), series were log-transformed and indices computed as residuals rather than ratios, avoiding the instability of the ratio index where the fitted curve approaches zero.”

```{r}

#' Detrend a long-format tree-ring dataframe with dplR
#'
#' @param data       A long-format data.frame/tibble with at least a year
#'   column, a sample/series id column, and the column to be detrended.
#' @param value_col  Name (string) of the column to detrend, e.g. "RW" or
#'   "Density".
#' @param year_col   Name (string) of the year column. Default "Year".
#' @param sample_col Name (string) of the sample/series id column.
#'   Default "Sample".
#' @param fill_method Method passed to `dplR::fill.internal.NA` for filling
#'   internal gaps before detrending (e.g. "Spline", "mean", "linear").
#'   Default "Spline".
#' @param detrend_method Method passed to `dplR::detrend`, e.g. "Spline",
#'   "ModNegExp", "Mean", "Ar", "Friedman", "AgeDepSpline". Default "Spline".
#' @param out_col    Name (string) of the new detrended column that is added
#'   to `data`. Default `paste0(value_col, "_Detrended")`.
#' @param ...        Extra arguments passed on to `dplR::detrend`
#'   (e.g. `nyrs = 50`, `f = 0.5`).
#'
#' @return `data` with one extra column (`out_col`) holding the detrended
#'   values. Rows where `value_col` was originally NA keep NA in `out_col`.
#'   Rows that fell inside a filled-in gap are dropped again after
#'   detrending, exactly like the manual pipeline in code_Main.Rmd.
#'
dplr_detrend_long <- function(data,
                              value_col,
                              year_col = "Year",
                              sample_col = "Sample",
                              fill_method = "Spline",
                              detrend_method = "Spline",
                              out_col = paste0(value_col, "_Detrended"),
                              ...) {
  
  stopifnot(value_col %in% names(data),
            year_col %in% names(data),
            sample_col %in% names(data))
  
  wide_input <- data[, c(year_col, sample_col, value_col)]
  names(wide_input) <- c("Year", "Sample", "Value")
  wide_input <- wide_input %>% filter(!is.na(Value))
  
  wide <- wide_input %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = "Sample", values_from = "Value") %>%
    arrange(Year) %>%
    complete(Year = seq(min(Year), max(Year), 1))
  
  years <- wide$Year
  wide$Year <- NULL
  wide <- as.data.frame(wide, check.names = FALSE)   # <-- the fix
  row.names(wide) <- years
  
  wide_filled <- fill.internal.NA(wide, fill = fill_method)
  detrended <- detrend(wide_filled, method = detrend_method, ...)
  
  # print(rwi.stats(detrended))
  # plot(time(detrended), sss(detrended),type="l",ylim=c(0.4,1),
  #      col="darkblue",lwd=2,xlab="Year",ylab="SSS")
  # abline(h=0.85,col="blue",lty="dashed")
  
  detrended$Year <- as.numeric(row.names(detrended))
  detrended_long <- pivot_longer(
    detrended,
    cols = -"Year",
    names_to = "Sample",
    values_to = out_col
  )
  
  result <- full_join(
    data, detrended_long,
    by = setNames(c("Year", "Sample"), c(year_col, sample_col))
  )
  
  result <- result[!is.na(result[[value_col]]), ]
  
  result
}



# log transform 
Data$logBBI <- log(Data$BBI_gmm *1000) # BBI in g/m


# detrend BBI residuals
Data <- dplr_detrend_long(
  data = Data,
  year_col = "Year",
  sample_col = "TreeID", 
  value_col = "logBBI",
  detrend_method = "Spline",
  nyrs = 30,
  out_col = "logBBI_detrended", 
  difference = TRUE
)
```

# make chronologies for each site and species

`CodeMain.qmd` grouped by `Species` alone, after filtering to Ghent. Here the
grouping is `Site x Species`, and the replication floor is `MIN_REPL` (see the
configuration chunk) rather than a hard-coded 10.

```{r chronologies}

ChronsAll <- Data %>%
  group_by(Site, Region, Species, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    BBI_chron = tbrm(logBBI_detrended),
    BBI_upper = tbrm(logBBI_detrended) + (qnorm(0.975)*sd(logBBI_detrended)/sqrt(n())),
    BBI_lower = tbrm(logBBI_detrended) - (qnorm(0.975)*sd(logBBI_detrended)/sqrt(n())),
    BBI_n = sum(!is.na(logBBI_detrended)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# what replication is actually available, before the floor is applied. This is
# the table to look at when deciding MIN_REPL: `max_n` is the best any year at
# that site x species can do.
ChronsAll %>%
  group_by(Site, Species) %>%
  summarise(
    max_n       = max(BBI_n),
    yrs_ge_repl = sum(BBI_n >= MIN_REPL & Year >= FIRST_YEAR),
    # guarded, because a site x species that never reaches MIN_REPL would
    # otherwise give min(integer(0)) = Inf and a warning
    first_yr    = if (any(BBI_n >= MIN_REPL)) min(Year[BBI_n >= MIN_REPL]) else NA_integer_,
    last_yr     = if (any(BBI_n >= MIN_REPL)) max(Year[BBI_n >= MIN_REPL]) else NA_integer_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  print(n = 30)

# cut at the replication floor and at the start of the instrumental record
ChronsAll <- ChronsAll %>%
  filter(BBI_n >= MIN_REPL, Year >= FIRST_YEAR)

# Drop site x species chronologies too short to reach MIN_N overlapping years
# in any window. Leaving them in produces an all-NA surface and then a
# "No rows for Chron = ..." error inside the plotting function, several
# minutes into the loop.
short <- ChronsAll %>%
  count(Site, Species) %>%
  filter(n < MIN_YEARS)

if (nrow(short)) {
  message("Dropping ", nrow(short), " chronolog", if (nrow(short) == 1) "y" else "ies",
          " shorter than MIN_YEARS = ", MIN_YEARS, ":")
  print(short)
  ChronsAll <- ChronsAll %>% anti_join(short, by = c("Site", "Species"))
}

ChronsAll %>%
  group_by(Site, Species) %>%
  summarise(n_years = n(), first_yr = min(Year), last_yr = max(Year),
            mean_n = round(mean(BBI_n), 1), .groups = "drop") %>%
  print(n = 30)


#### figure: every chronology, one row per site ####

chronplot <- ggplot(ChronsAll, aes(x = Year)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = BBI_chron), colour = "red", linewidth = 0.4) +

  facet_grid(Site ~ Species, scales = "free_y") +
```
